turns.assessment: The stated degradation on svc156 is not corroborated by any recorded symptom. Optical PM on relevant line interfaces and channel monitors is unchanged, and numerous healthy services share its working route; the sole observation is a small OSNR increase at S19 on an unrelated S18-S19 line, 360 s after the estimated onset. Receiver-local degradation, channel-specific WSS filtering, or gradual margin erosion remain possible, but the evidence cannot localize or strongly support any of them.

proposals.rationale: A receiver-local penalty could affect only svc156 while shared optical facilities and neighboring services remain normal. However, no receiver PM degradation was observed, so support is weak.

A channel-specific passband shift can reduce signal quality without changing power or affecting other channels. No corresponding endpoint quality change was recorded, and there is no evidence identifying a particular ROADM.
Channel margin erosion could present as degraded quality without a shared-path impact, but it is normally reported at a receiver and no such PM change was found.

score.why: cause flagged as unconsidered and absent
